qt: to the Commission Nikolas Farantouris (S&D) Subject:

On 1 October 2026, the European Commission sent Greece a letter of formal notice1 for failing to comply with the judgment of the CJEU of 19 June 20252, which found the country to be in breach of Directive 2011/7/EU3 due to excessive delays in payments by public hospitals to their suppliers. In fact, according to the most recent available figures, in August 2026 the State owed private businesses more than EUR 3.8 billion. Hospitals continue to top the list of debtors, followed by social security funds, local authorities and other public legal entities4. These delays carry a heavy financial toll for suppliers, most of whom are small and mediumsized businesses, compromising their functioning, growth and liquidity and triggering a chain reaction in the economy. Meanwhile, the Greek Government is stepping up its scheme to recover money owed to the State. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
What specific compliance measures is it demanding that the Greek Government take to address these systematic delays?

What is its assessment of the Greek Government’s measures so far and does it consider that the recently announced digital platform Synepeia5 is enough to put an immediate stop to systemic late payments?
What protection measures does it plan to put forward to ease the suffocating pressure on private businesses resulting from the Greek State’s failure to pay its bills on time?
